findings.title: Midnight timestamps are silently expanded into whole-day bounds
findings.description:
The `date | datetime` union parses midnight timestamp strings as dates, losing their time and timezone before `resolve_window()` runs. Reproduced through the actual route: `end=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` reaches the reader as `2026-06-01T23:59:59.999999Z`. Both endpoints therefore return rows outside explicitly requested windows; offset-midnight timestamps also lose their offset.

Distinguish bare dates from timestamps before coercion. Add route tests covering midnight timestamps, timezone offsets, and bare-date expansion.

findings.title: Large response construction and serialization block the event loop
findings.description:
Only database reads run in the executor. `CandlesResponse.build()` and `timeseries_response()` then execute synchronously on the event loop. The trades handler repeats this at lines 166–174.

Using the permitted 75,000 candle rows, local measurement took approximately **714 ms building models plus 548 ms serializing**, blocking other requests on that worker for roughly 1.26 seconds. This violates the explicit async execution rule despite releasing the database connection first.

Move model construction and serialization into executor work after releasing the connection. Add a concurrent responsiveness test while serving a ceiling-sized response; the existing concurrency test exercises only market-detail requests.
